availableCommands.name: animation-vocabulary
availableCommands.description: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one. (user)

availableCommands.name: ask-matt
availableCommands.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. (user)

availableCommands.name: code-review
availableCommands.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X". (user)

availableCommands.name: codebase-design
availableCommands.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary. (user)

availableCommands.name: diagnosing-bugs
availableCommands.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow. (user)

availableCommands.name: domain-modeling
availableCommands.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model. (user)

availableCommands.name: emil-design-eng
availableCommands.description: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great. (user)

availableCommands.name: find-animation-opportunities
availableCommands.description: Search a codebase or UI for places that don't animate but should, and reject everything that shouldn't. Read-only; it proposes motion with exact values, it does not implement it. Use when the user asks "what could be animated here?" or wants to "make this feel more alive". For fixing existing animations, use improve-animations or review-animations instead. (user)

availableCommands.name: find-skills
availableCommands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill. (user)

availableCommands.name: grill-me

availableCommands.name: grill-with-docs
availableCommands.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go. (user)

availableCommands.name: grilling

availableCommands.name: handoff

availableCommands.name: improve-codebase-architecture

availableCommands.name: prototype

availableCommands.name: research

availableCommands.name: resolving-merge-conflicts

availableCommands.name: review-animations

availableCommands.name: tdd

availableCommands.name: triage

availableCommands.name: usage-bar

availableCommands.name: vercel-composition-patterns

Triggers on tasks involving React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle optimization, or performance improvements. (user)

availableCommands.description: Stop. That last message did not land — re-pitch it. (user)

availableCommands.name: wayfinder
availableCommands.description: Plan a huge chunk of work — more than one agent session can hold — as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear. (user)

availableCommands.name: wizard

Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself. (user)
